info.title: egdata.app API
info.description: REST API for Epic Games Store catalog, pricing, search, and public egdata.app data. Public access at https://api.egdata.app is unchanged while the Worker gateway is staged separately. The dedicated origin-api.egdata.app hostname requires a private Worker-to-origin credential; direct requests return 403 ORIGIN_ACCESS_DENIED (or 503 ORIGIN_NOT_CONFIGURED if the origin lacks configuration). Clients must not send or obtain X-Egdata-Origin-Token. Global origin enforcement and moving the public hostname to the Worker require a separate explicit cutover. This contract starts with public stable REST endpoints and will expand as legacy routes are classified. The separately documented GraphQL endpoint defaults to 30 POST requests per minute per client IP (RATE_LIMIT_GRAPHQL_POST_PER_MINUTE); exceeding the quota returns 429 with Retry-After. GraphQL GET/APQ has a separate default quota of 1200 per minute.

post.summary: Initialize or solve a proof-of-work session challenge
post.description: Send {} to receive a signed challenge. Solve SHA-256(challenge + ':' + nonce) with the returned leading-zero bit difficulty, then POST {challenge, nonce} to receive a ten-minute session. Invalid/expired proofs return a fresh challenge with HTTP 200. Enabled in observe/enforce modes. No account login is required. Fingerprint v2 preserves header order while excluding Apollo/CORS plumbing; changing fingerprint versions invalidates old bound tokens. CORS preflight max-age is 600 seconds for allowed origins (HTTPS egdata.app/subdomains and explicit integration/development origins). Behavior scoring collapses hydration/typeahead and includes distinct-title sweeps within a bounded 60-second window; deep-only access alone adds no risk.

post.summary: Hydrate catalog records for known technical identifiers
post.description:
Resolves up to 25 item, asset, or release-app roots directly from the catalog collections. The response is NDJSON with one isolated, content-hashed graph result per line.

When ANTI_ABUSE_MODE=enforce, clients with current risk <= 0.5 can request data without a PoW session. Only suspicious clients (0.5 < risk <= 0.8) require a valid session less than 30 seconds old; missing, invalid, or expired sessions return SESSION_CHALLENGE_REQUIRED with HTTP 200. Clients can solve PoW on demand and retry once. Scores above 0.8 receive a 3–5 second delay and HTTP 204 No Content with X-Egdata-Mitigation: tarpit regardless of session. Historical token scores do not prevent recovery after current risk clears. Normal responses retain existing cache policies and ETags; challenges, bodyless tarpits and canary lists are private/no-store. Baseline rate limits remain active and can return 429. Cloudflare cache hits bypass origin scoring and require separate edge controls. Existing account authentication requirements still apply. In observe mode an operator can apply the same policy to exact trusted fingerprints on offer-detail or catalog-search routes for an expiring trial of at most 15 minutes. Catalog search and sandbox-offer pagination contribute traversal evidence, grouped by normalized filters; ordinary isolated queries remain low-risk.

When accessed through the Worker gateway with an API key, this operation consumes the project's shared UTC-aligned 60-second quota across all keys, console sessions, and legacy/v1 gateway requests. Free: 120/min; pro: 1200/min; enterprise: 6000/min, overridden by approved project RPM. Cache hits count. Exhaustion returns 429 RATE_LIMITED; unavailable admission returns 503 QUOTA_UNAVAILABLE with Retry-After: 1. Gateway errors use { error: { code, message } }. Public unauthenticated bypasses retain their existing behavior.
